chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whose enemy met him and acquired wealth or chattels from him, then the Muslims acquired that. How should one deal with the chattels of the man? He said: If they acquired it before they had possessed the man's chattels, it is returned to him; and if they acquired it after having possessed it, then it is war booty (fa'i) for the Muslims, and he has the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah).

key_terms.فَيْ‏ءٌ: war booty or spoils acquired without battle
key_terms.يَحُوزُوا: to possess or take hold of

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on property taken by an enemy and then recovered by Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between individual recovery and communal booty (fa'i) based on the timing of formal possession (huzūm) by the Muslim army. It establishes that if the enemy had already secured the item before the Muslims' main force took control, it remains the private property of the original owner; otherwise, it becomes communal property, granting the owner the right of pre-emption (shuf'a) to reclaim it. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the precise moment of transfer of ownership during military campaigns.
